properties.name: Work that drifted can be frozen without freezing the work that did not
properties.statement: reflow2's response to unacceptable drift is all-or-nothing. tools/reflow2_check.py thresholds WHICH findings count — anchored gaps at or above --gap-threshold (default 0.8) fail the build — but the response is a single sys.exit(1) and the whole build goes red. There is no state in which some capabilities are frozen pending a decision while the rest of the work proceeds. reflow could do this. Its rigid-mode resync offered the user two options, and option B was: "Document each drift item as change request, add to context/change_requests.json, BLOCK implementation of drifted features, continue with non-drifted work." The RESYNC_to_P1 path for major drift in rigid mode likewise says "BLOCK until change request approved" — a targeted freeze, not a stopped project. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS. On a system being evolved incrementally against functional production code — Anthony's actual case at NSLS-II, a ten-year-old bluesky stack evolving on the fly — "stop everything until this is resolved" is almost never the right answer, and "carry on regardless" is never the right answer either. Partial blocking is the only response that matches how the work actually proceeds: quarantine what is contested, keep delivering what is not. It is also what makes a gate survivable in a shared repo, where one contested capability currently reddens the build for everyone. WHAT reflow2 ALREADY HAS, so this is a smaller change than it appears: the graph can already say which capabilities are affected (propagate_change gives the blast radius; scope + claim_region give "the part I hold"), and status/proposed already expresses "not agreed yet". What is missing is that nothing READS those to scope a refusal — the gate asks one global question and gives one global answer. OPEN: whether a partial block is advisory (reported, not enforced, per dec:report-dont-judge) or actually refuses writes against the frozen region, and whether the frozen set is computed from the drift's blast radius or named by the user. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows. Anthony's word: capture it.
